quotes.quote: If a person gave away your body to some passerby, you'd be furious. Yet you hand over your mind to anyone who comes along, so they may abuse you, leaving it disturbed and troubled—have you no shame in that?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: The unrestricted person, who has in hand what they will in all events, is free. But anyone who can be restricted, coerced, or pushed into something against what they will is a slave.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Whenever you find yourself blaming providence, turn it around in your mind and you will see that what has happened is in keeping with reason.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: You are not your body and hair-style, but your capacity for choosing well. If your choices are beautiful, so too will you be.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: For there are two rules to keep at the ready—that there is nothing good or bad outside my own reasoned choice, and that we shouldn't try to lead events but to follow them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: What is it then to be properly educated? It is learning to apply our natural preconceptions to the right things according to Nature, and beyond that to separate the things that lie within our power from those that don't.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: First off, don't let the force of the impression carry you away. Say to it, 'hold up a bit and let me see who you are and where you are from—let me put you to the test'...
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It isn't events themselves that disturb people, but only their judgements about them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: First tell yourself what kind of person you want to be, then do what you have to do. For in nearly every pursuit we see this to be the case. Those in athletic pursuit first choose the sport they want, and then do that work.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: We don't abandon our pursuits because we despair of ever perfecting them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: You can bind up my leg, but not even Zeus has the power to break my freedom of choice.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It is easy to praise providence for anything that may happen if you have two qualities: a complete view of what has actually happened in each instance and a sense of gratitude. Without gratitude what is the point of seeing, and without seeing what is the object of gratitude?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Don't trust in your reputation, money, or position, but in the strength that is yours—namely, your judgments about the things that you control and don't control. For this alone is what makes us free and unfettered, that picks us up by the neck from the depths and lifts us eye to eye with the rich and powerful.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: In short, you must remember this—that if you hold anything dear outside of your own reasoned choice, you will have destroyed your capacity for choice.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: The key is to keep company only with people who uplift you, whose presence calls forth your best.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Misfortunes test friends and detect enemies.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Strengthen yourself with contentment, for it is an impregnable fortress.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: All philosophy lies in two words, sustain and abstain.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: All religions must be tolerated... for every man must get to heaven in his own way.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Be careful to leave your sons well instructed rather than rich, for the hopes of the instructed are better than the wealth of the ignorant.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Control thy passions lest they take vengence on thee.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Do not laugh much or often or unrestrainedly.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Do not seek to bring things to pass in accordance with your wishes, but wish for them as they are, and you will find them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: First learn the meaning of what you say, and then speak.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Freedom is not procured by a full enjoyment of what is desired, but by controlling the desire.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: He is a drunkard who takes more than three glasses though he be not drunk.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If evil be spoken of you and it be true, correct yourself, if it be a lie, laugh at it.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If one oversteps the bounds of moderation, the greatest pleasures cease to please.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If thy brother wrongs thee, remember not so much his wrong-doing, but more than ever that he is thy brother.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If virtue promises happiness, prosperity and peace, then progress in virtue is progress in each of these for to whatever point the perfection of anything brings us, progress is always an approach toward it.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Imagine for yourself a character, a model personality, whose example you determine to follow, in private as well as in public.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Is freedom anything else than the right to live as we wish? Nothing else.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It is not he who reviles or strikes you who insults you, but your opinion that these things are insulting.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It is the nature of the wise to resist pleasures, but the foolish to be a slave to them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It takes more than just a good looking body. You've got to have the heart and soul to go with it.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Never in any case say I have lost such a thing, but I have returned it. Is your child dead? It is a return. Is your wife dead? It is a return. Are you deprived of your estate? Is not this also a return?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: No great thing is created suddenly.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Nothing great is created suddenly, any more than a bunch of grapes or a fig. If you tell me that you desire a fig. I answer you that there must be time. Let it first blossom, then bear fruit, then ripen.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Only the educated are free.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Silence is safer than speech.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: The essence of philosophy is that a man should so live that his happiness shall depend as little as possible on external things.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: The two powers which in my opinion constitute a wise man are those of bearing and forbearing.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: There is nothing good or evil save in the will.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: To accuse others for one's own misfortunes is a sign of want of education. To accuse oneself shows that one's education has begun. To accuse neither oneself nor others shows that one's education is complete.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Unless we place our religion and our treasure in the same thing, religion will always be sacrificed.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: We tell lies, yet it is easy to show that lying is immoral.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Whenever you are angry, be assured that it is not only a present evil, but that you have increased a habit.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Whoever does not regard what he has as most ample wealth, is unhappy, though he be master of the world.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: You may be always victorious if you will never enter into any contest where the issue does not wholly depend upon yourself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: A city is not adorned by external things, but by the virtue of those who dwell in it.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Adopt new habits yourself: consolidate your principles by putting them into practice.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: A guide, on finding a man who has lost his way, brings him back to the right path-he does not mock and jeer at him and then take himself off. You also must show the unlearned man the truth, and you will see that he will follow. But so long as you do not show it him, you should not mock, but rather feel your own incapacity.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: An ignorant person is inclined to blame others for his own misfortune. To blame oneself is proof of progress. But the wise man never has to blame another or himself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: An uninstructed person will lay the fault of his own bad condition upon others. Someone just starting instruction will lay the fault on himself. Some who is perfectly instructed will place blame neither on others nor on himself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: As a man, casting off worn out garments taketh new ones, so the dweller in the body, entereth into ones that are new.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: A ship should not ride on a single anchor, nor life on a single hope.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Asked, Who is the rich man? Epictetus replied, He who is content.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: As the sun does not wait for prayers and incantations to be induced to rise, but immediately shines and is saluted by all, so do you also not wait for clappings of hands and shouts of praise to be induced to do good, but be a doer of good voluntarily and you will be beloved as much as the sun.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Attach yourself to what is spiritually superior, regardless of what other people think or do. Hold to your true aspirations no matter what is going on around you.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Be free from grief not through insensibility like the irrational animals, nor through want of thought like the foolish, but like a man of virtue by having reason as the consolation of grief.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Caretake this moment. Immerse yourself in its particulars. Respond to this person, this challenge, this deed. Quit the evasions. Stop giving yourself needless trouble. It is time to really live; to fully inhabit the situation you happen to be in now. You are not some disinterested bystander. Participate. Exert yourself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Circumstances do not rise to meet our expectations. Events happen as they do. People behave as they are. Embrace what you actually get.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Circumstances don't make the man, they only reveal him to himself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Conduct yourself in all matters, grand and public or small and domestic, in accordance with the laws of nature. Harmonizing your will with nature should be your utmost ideal.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Crows pick out the eyes of the dead, when the dead have no longer need of them; but flatterers mar the soul of the living, and her eyes they blind.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Death is not dreadful or else it would have appeared dreadful to Socrates.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Difficulty shows what men are. Therefore when a difficulty falls upon you, remember that God, like a trainer of wrestlers, has matched you with a rough young man. Why? So that you may become an Olympic conqueror; but it is not accomplished without sweat.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Does anyone bathe hastily? Do not say that they do it ill, but hastily. Does anyone drink much wine? Do not say that they do ill, but that they drink a great deal. For unless you perfectly understand their motives, how should you know if they act ill? Thus you will not risk yielding to any appearances except those you fully comprehend.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: [Do not get too attached to life] for it is like a sailor's leave on the shore and at any time, the captain may sound the horn, calling you back to eternal darkness.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Don't explain your philosophy. Embody it.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Don't hope that events will turn out the way you want, welcome events in whichever way they happen: this is the path to peace.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Don't live by your own rules, but in harmony with nature.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Don't put your purpose in one place and expect to see progress made somewhere else.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Either God wants to abolish evil, and cannot; or he can, but does not want to.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Events do not just happen, but arrive by appointment.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Everyone's life is a warfare, and that long and various.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Finally, when he crowns it off by becoming a senator, then he becomes a slave in fine company, then he experiences the poshest and most prestigious form of enslavement.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: For even sheep do not vomit up their grass and show to the shepherds how much they have eaten; but when they have internally digested the pasture, they produce externally wool and milk. Do you also show not your theorems to the uninstructed, but show the acts which come from their digestion.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: For I am not Eternity, but a human being-a part of the whole, as an hour is part of the day. I must come like the hour, and like the hour must pass!
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: For if we had any sense, what else should we do, both in public and in private, than sing hymns and praise the deity, and recount all the favours that he has conferred!
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: For it is not death or pain that is to be feared, but the fear of pain or death.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: For what else is tragedy than the portrayal in tragic verse of the sufferings of men who have attached high value to external things?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: For where you find unrest, grief, fear, frustrated desire, failed aversion, jealousy and envy, happiness has no room for admittance. And where values are false, these passions inevitably follow.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Freedom is secured not by the fulfilling of men's desires, but by the removal of desire.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Freedom is the only worthy goal in life. It is won by disregarding things that lie beyond our control.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Free is the person who lives as he wishes and cannot be coerced, impeded or compelled, whose impulses cannot be thwarted, who always gets what he desires and never has to experience what he would rather avoid.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: God has entrusted me with myself. No man is free who is not master of himself. A man should so live that his happiness shall depend as little as possible on external things. The world turns aside to let any man pass who knows where he is going.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: God save me from fools with a little philosophy-no one is more difficult to reach.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Here are thieves and robbers and tribunals: and they that are called tyrants, who deem that they have after a fashion power over us, because of the miserable body and what appertains to it. Let us show them that they have power over none.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: He who exercises wisdom, exercises the knowledge which is about God.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: He who is discontented with what he has, and with what has been granted to him by fortune, is one who is ignorant of the art of living, but he who bears that in a noble spirit, and makes reasonable use of all that comes from it, deserves to be regarded as a good man.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: He who laughs at himself never runs out of things to laugh at.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If any be unhappy, let him remember that he is unhappy by reason of himself alone. For God hath made all men to enjoy felicity and constancy of good.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If anyone tells you that a certain person speaks ill of you, do not make excuses about what is said of you but answer, "He was ignorant of my other faults, else he would not have mentioned these alone."
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If they are wise, do not quarrel with them; if they are fools, ignore them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If you choose, you are free; if you choose, you need blame no man-accuse no man. All things will be at once according to your mind and according to the Mind of God.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If you ever happen to turn your attention to externals, for the pleasure of any one, be assured that you have ruined your scheme of life. Be contented, then, in everything, with being a philosopher; and if you with to seem so likewise to any one, appear so to yourself, and it will suffice you.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If you have assumed a character above your strength, you have both acted in this matter in an unbecoming way, and you have neglected that which you might have fulfilled.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If you wish it, you are free; if you wish it, you'll find fault with no one, you'll cast blame on no one, and everything that comes about will do so in accordance with your own will and that of God.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If you wish to be good, first believe that you are bad.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: If you would cure anger, do not feed it. Say to yourself: 'I used to be angry every day; then every other day; now only every third or fourth day.' When you reach thirty days offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the gods.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: I laugh at those who think they can damage me. They do not know who I am, they do not know what I think, they cannot even touch the things which are really mine and with which I live.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: I must die. Must I then die lamenting? I must be put in chains. Must I then also lament? I must go into exile. Does any man then hinder me from going with smiles and cheerfulness and contentment?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: In banquets remember that you entertain two guests, body and soul: and whatever you shall have given to the body you soon eject: but what you shall have given to the soul, you keep always.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: In literature, too, it is not great achievement to memorize what you have read while not formulating an opinion of your own.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Is then the fruit of a fig-tree not perfect suddenly and in one hour, and would you possess the fruit of a man's mind in so short a time and so easily?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It has been ordained that there be summer and winter, abundance and dearth, virtue and vice, and all such opposites for the harmony of the whole, and (Zeus) has given each of us a body, property, and companions.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It is always our choice whether or not we wish to pay the price for life's rewards. And often it is best for us not to pay the price, for the price might be our integrity.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It is a universal law - have no illusion - that every creature alive is attached to nothing so much as to its own self-interest.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It is better to die of hunger having lived without grief and fear, than to live with a troubled spirit, amid abundance.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It is better to do wrong seldom and to own it, and to act right for the most part, than seldom to admit that you have done wrong and to do wrong often.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It is our attitude toward events, not events themselves, which we can control. Nothing is by its own nature calamitous - even death is terrible only if we fear it.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: It is unrealistic to expect people to see you as you see yourself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Keep the prospect of death, exile and all such apparent tragedies before you every day - especially death - and you will never have an abject thought, or desire anything to excess.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Know you not that a good man does nothing for appearance sake, but for the sake of having done right?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Let silence be your general rule; or say only what is necessary and in few words.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Let your will to avoid have no concern with what is not in man's power; direct it only to things in man's power that are contrary to nature.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Man is troubled not by events, but by the meaning he gives to them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Many people who have progressively lowered their personal standards in an attempt to win social acceptance and life's comforts bitterly resent those of philosophical bent who refuse to compromise their spiritual ideals and who seek to better themselves.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Men are disturbed not by the things that happen, but by their opinion of the things that happen.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Nature hath given men one tongue but two ears, that we may hear from others twice as much as we speak.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Never praise or blame people on common grounds; look to their judgements exclusively. Because that is the determining factor, which makes everyone's actions either good or bad.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Never say about anything, I have lost it, but only I have given it back.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: No one is ever unhappy because of someone else.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: On the occasion of every accident that befalls you, remember to turn to yourself and inquire what power you have for turning it to use.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Other people's views and troubles can be contagious. Don't sabotage yourself by unwittingly adopting negative, unproductive attitudes through your associations with others.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Preach not to others what they should eat, but eat as becomes you and be silent.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Protect what belongs to you at all costs; don't desire what belongs to another.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Reading should serve the goal of attaining peace; if it doesn't make you peaceful, what good is it?
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Remember from now on whenever something tends to make you unhappy, draw on this principle: 'This is no misfortune; but bearing with it bravely is a blessing.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Restrict yourself to choice and refusal; and exercise them carefully, with discipline and detachment.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Seek not the good in external things; seek it in yourselves.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Sickness is a problem for the body, not the mind - unless the mind decides that it is a problem. Lameness, too, is the body's problem, not the mind's. Say this to yourself whatever the circumstance and you will find without fail that the problem pertains to something else, not to you.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Small-minded people blame others. Average people blame themselves. The wise see all blame as foolishness.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: So don't make a show of your philosophical learning to the uninitiated, show them by your actions what you have absorbed.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: So if you like doing something, do it regularly; if you don't like doing something, make a habit of doing something different.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: So what oppresses and scares us? It is our own thoughts, obviously, What overwhelms people when they are about to leaves friends, family, old haunts and their accustomed way of life? Thoughts.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: So you wish to conquer in the Olympic Games, my friend? And I, too... But first mark the conditions and the consequences. You will have to put yourself under discipline; to eat by rule, to avoid cakes and sweetmeats; to take exercise at the appointed hour whether you like it or not, in cold and heat; to abstain from cold drinks and wine at your will. Then, in the conflict itself you are likely enough to dislocate your wrist or twist your ankle, to swallow a great deal of dust, to be severely thrashed, and after all of these things, to be defeated.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Take care not to hurt the ruling faculty of your mind. If you were to guard against this in every action, you should enter upon those actions more safely.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Tentative efforts lead to tentative outcomes. Therefore, give yourself fully to your endeavors. Decide to construct your character through excellent actions and determine to pay the price of a worthy goal. The trials you encounter will introduce you to your strengths. Remain steadfast and one day you will build something that endures: something worthy of your potential.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: The condition and characteristic of an uninstructed person is this: he never expects from himself profit (advantage) nor harm, but from externals. The condition and characteristic of a philosopher is this: he expects all advantage and all harm from himself.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: The gods do not exists, and even if they exist they do not trouble themselves about people, and we have nothing in common with them. The piety and devotion to the gods that the majority of people invoke is a lie devised by swindlers and con men and, if you can believe it, by legislators, to keep criminals in line by putting the fear of God into them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: The greater the difficulty, the more glory in surmounting it. Skillful pilots gain their reputation from storms and tempests.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: The more we value things outside our control, the less control we have.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: The philosopher's school, ye men, is a surgery: you ought not to go out of it with pleasure, but with pain. For you are not in sound health when you enter.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: There is a time and place for diversion and amusements, but you should never allow them to override your true purposes.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: There is but one way to tranquility of mind and happiness, and that is to account no external things thine own, but to commit all to God.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: There is no shame in making an honest effort.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: These reasoning's do not cohere: I am richer than you, therefore I am better than you; I am more eloquent than you, therefore I am better than you. On the contrary these rather cohere, I am richer than you, therefore my possessions are greater than yours: I am more eloquent than you, therefore my speech is superior to yours. But you are neither possession nor speech.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: To admonish is better than to reproach for admonition is mild and friendly, but reproach is harsh and insulting; and admonition corrects those who are doing wrong, but reproach only convicts them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: To Epictetus, all external events are determined by fate, and are thus beyond our control, but we can accept whatever happens calmly and dispassionately. Individuals, however, are responsible for their own actions which they can examine and control through rigorous self-discipline. Suffering arises from trying to control what is uncontrollable, or from neglecting what is within our power. As part of the universal city that is the universe, human beings have a duty of care to all fellow humans. The person who followed these precepts would achieve happiness.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Very little is needed for everything to be upset and ruined, only a slight lapse in reason.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: We are at the mercy of whoever wields authority over the things we either desire or detest. If you would be free, then, do not wish to have, or avoid, things that other people control, because then you must serve as their slave.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: We are not disturbed by what happens to us, but by our thoughts about what happens to us.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: We cannot choose our external circumstances, but we can always choose how we respond to them.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: We should realize that an opinion is not easily formed unless a person says and hears the same things every day and practises them in real life.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: What are we to do, then? To make the best of what lies within our power, and deal with everything else as it comes. 'How does it come, then?' As God wills.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: What concerns me is not the way things are, but the way people think things are.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: What you shun enduring yourself, attempt not to impose on others. You shun slavery - beware enslaving others! If you can endure to do that, one would think you had been once upon a time a slave yourself. For vice has nothing in common with virtue, nor Freedom with slavery.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: When a youth was giving himself airs in the Theatre and saying, 'I am wise, for I have conversed with many wise men,' Epictetus replied, 'I too have conversed with many rich men, yet I am not rich!'.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: Whenever anyone criticizes or wrongs you, remember that they are only doing or saying what they think is right. They cannot be guided by your views, only their own; so if their views are wrong, they are the ones who suffer insofar as they are misguided.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: When then any man assents to that which is false, be assured that he did not intend to assent to it as false, for every soul is unwillingly deprived of the truth, as Plato says; but the falsity seemed to him to be true.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.quote: When things seem to have reached that stage, merely say "I won't play any longer", and take your departure; but if you stay, stop lamenting.

quotes.quote: To think is easy. To act is difficult. To act as one thinks is the most difficult of all.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Nothing is worth more than this day.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Fools and the wise are equally harmless. It is the half-fools and the half-wise that are dangerous.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: As we are constituted by nature, there is not a fault that could not turn into a virtue, not a virtue that could not turn into a fault.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Nature goes her way, and all that to us seems an exception is really according to order.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: One should, every day at least, hear a little song, read a good poem, see a fine picture, and, if possible, speak a few reasonable words.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: A clever man commits no minor blunders.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: A correct answer is like an affectionate kiss.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: A creation of importance can only be produced when its author isolates himself, it is a child of solitude.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: A man's manners are a mirror in which he shows his portrait.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: A noble person attracts noble people, and knows how to hold on to them.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: A person hears only what they understand.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: A person places themselves on a level with the ones they praise.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: All intelligent thoughts have already been thought; what is necessary is only to try to think them again.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: All the knowledge I possess everyone else can acquire, but my heart is all my own.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: All theory, dear friend, is gray, but the golden tree of life springs ever green.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: All things are only transitory.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: An unused life is an early death.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Be above it! Make the world serve your purpose, but do not serve it.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Be generous with kindly words, especially about those who are absent.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Beauty is a manifestation of secret natural laws, which otherwise would have been hidden from us forever.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Beauty is everywhere a welcome guest.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Behaviour is the mirror in which everyone shows their image.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Being brilliant is no great feat if you respect nothing.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Certain defects are necessary for the existence of individuality.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Character, in great and little things, means carrying through what you feel able to do.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Common sense is the genius of humanity.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Daring ideas are like chessmen moved forward; they may be beaten, but they may start a winning game.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Death is a commingling of eternity with time; in the death of a good man, eternity is seen looking through time.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Deeply earnest and thoughtful people stand on shaky footing with the public.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Destiny grants us our wishes, but in its own way, in order to give us something beyond our wishes.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Divide and rule, the politician cries; unite and lead, is watchword of the wise.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Do not give in too much to feelings. A overly sensitive heart is an unhappy possession on this shaky earth.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Doubt grows with knowledge.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Dream no small dreams for they have no power to move the hearts of men.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Every author in some way portrays himself in his works, even if it be against his will.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Every person above the ordinary has a certain mission that they are called to fulfill.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Every spoken word arouses our self-will.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Every step of life shows much caution is required.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Everybody wants to be somebody; nobody wants to grow.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Everything in the world may be endured except continual prosperity.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Few people have the imagination for reality.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: For a man to achieve all that is demanded of him he must regard himself as greater than he is.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Fresh activity is the only means of overcoming adversity.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Go to foreign countries and you will get to know the good things one possesses at home.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Great thoughts and a pure heart, that is what we should ask from God.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Happiness is a ball after which we run wherever it rolls, and we push it with our feet when it stops.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Hatred is active, and envy passive dislike; there is but one step from envy to hate.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Hatred is something peculiar. You will always find it strongest and most violent where there is the lowest degree of culture.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: He is dead in this world who has no belief in another.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: He is happiest, be he king or peasant, who finds peace in his home.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: He only earns his freedom and his life Who takes them every day by storm.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: He who does not think much of himself is much more esteemed than he imagines.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: He who enjoys doing and enjoys what he has done is happy.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: He who has a task to perform must know how to take sides, or he is quite unworthy of it.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: He who possesses art and science has religion; he who does not possess them, needs religion.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: I can tell you, honest friend, what to believe: believe life; it teaches better that book or orator.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: I do not know myself, and God forbid that I should.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: I love those who yearn for the impossible.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: I never knew a more presumptuous person than myself. The fact that I say that shows that what I say is true.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: I think that I am better than the people who are trying to reform me.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: I will listen to anyone's convictions, but pray keep your doubts to yourself.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: If God had wanted me otherwise, He would have created me otherwise.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: If I love you, what business is it of yours?
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: If a man writes a book, let him set down only what he knows. I have guesses enough of my own.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: If children grew up according to early indications, we should have nothing but geniuses.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: If you modestly enjoy your fame you are not unworthy to rank with the holy.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: If you start to think of your physical and moral condition, you usually find that you are sick.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: If you wish to know the mind of a man, listen to his words.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: If your treat an individual... as if he were what he ought to be and could be, he will become what he ought to be and could be.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Ignorant men raise questions that wise men answered a thousand years ago.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: In art the best is good enough.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: In nature we never see anything isolated, but everything in connection with something else which is before it, beside it, under it and over it.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: In the realm of ideas everything depends on enthusiasm... in the real world all rests on perseverance.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: It is after all the greatest art to limit and isolate oneself.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: It is better to be deceived by one's friends than to deceive them.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: It is in self-limitation that a master first shows himself.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: It is not doing the thing we like to do, but liking the thing we have to do, that makes life blessed.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: It is the strange fate of man, that even in the greatest of evils the fear of the worst continues to haunt him.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: It seems to never occur to fools that merit and good fortune are closely united.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Know thyself? If I knew myself I would run away.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Let everyone sweep in front of his own door, and the whole world will be clean.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Letters are among the most significant memorial a person can leave behind them.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Life belongs to the living, and he who lives must be prepared for changes.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Life is the childhood of our immortality.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Live dangerously and you live right.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Love and desire are the spirit's wings to great deeds.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Love can do much, but duty more.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Love does not dominate; it cultivates.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Magic is believing in yourself, if you can do that, you can make anything happen.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Man is made by his belief. As he believes, so he is.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Many people take no care of their money till they come nearly to the end of it, and others do just the same with their time.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Mastery passes often for egotism.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Music is either sacred or secular. The sacred agrees with its dignity, and here has its greatest effect on life, an effect that remains the same through all ages and epochs. Secular music should be cheerful throughout.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Nature knows no pause in progress and development, and attaches her curse on all inaction.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: No one has ever learned fully to know themselves.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: No one would talk much in society if they knew how often they misunderstood others.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: None are more hopelessly enslaved than those who falsely believe they are free.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Nothing is more fearful than imagination without taste.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Nothing is more terrible than to see ignorance in action.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Nothing is to be rated higher than the value of the day.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Nothing shows a man's character more than what he laughs at.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Objects in pictures should so be arranged as by their very position to tell their own story.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: On all the peaks lies peace.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: One always has time enough, if one will apply it well.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: One can be instructed in society, one is inspired only in solitude.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: One cannot develop taste from what is of average quality but only from the very best.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: One must ask children and birds how cherries and strawberries taste.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Only by joy and sorrow does a person know anything about themselves and their destiny. They learn what to do and what to avoid.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Passions are vices or virtues to their highest powers.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Personality is everything in art and poetry.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Piety is not a goal but a means to attain through the purest peace of mind the highest culture.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Precaution is better than cure.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Science arose from poetry... when times change the two can meet again on a higher level as friends.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Self-knowledge comes from knowing other men.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Sowing is not as difficult as reaping.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Talent develops in quiet places, character in the full current of human life.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Talk well of the absent whenever you have the opportunity.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The artist alone sees spirits. But after he has told of their appearing to him, everybody sees them.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The biggest problem with every art is by the use of appearance to create a loftier reality.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The coward only threatens when he is safe.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The decline of literature indicates the decline of a nation.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The deed is everything, the glory is naught.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The formation of one's character ought to be everyone's chief aim.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The hardest thing to see is what is in front of your eyes.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The human mind will not be confined to any limits.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The intelligent man finds almost everything ridiculous, the sensible man hardly anything.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The little man is still a man.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The man who occupies the first place seldom plays the principal part.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The man with insight enough to admit his limitations comes nearest to perfection.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The mediator of the inexpressible is the work of art.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The most happy man is he who knows how to bring into relation the end and beginning of his life.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The people who are absent are the ideal; those who are present seem to be quite commonplace.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The right man is the one who seizes the moment.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The soul that sees beauty may sometimes walk alone.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The unnatural, that too is natural.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The world remains ever the same.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: There is a courtesy of the heart; it is allied to love. From its springs the purest courtesy in the outward behavior.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: There is nothing in the world more shameful than establishing one's self on lies and fables.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: There is nothing in which people more betray their character than in what they laugh at.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: There is nothing insignificant in the world. It all depends on the point of view.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: There is nothing so terrible as activity without insight.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Thinking is more interesting than knowing, but less interesting than looking.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: This is the highest wisdom that I own; freedom and life are earned by those alone who conquer them each day anew.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Those who hope for no other life are dead even for this.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: To appreciate the noble is a gain which can never be torn from us.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: To create something you must be something.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: To rule is easy, to govern difficult.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: To the person with a firm purpose all men and things are servants.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: To witness two lovers is a spectacle for the gods.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Unlike grown ups, children have little need to deceive themselves.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Upon the creatures we have made, we are, ourselves, at last, dependent.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: We are never further from what we wish than when we believe that we have what we wished for.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: We cannot fashion our children after our desires, we must have them and love them as God has given them to us.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: We don't get to know people when they come to us; we must go to them to find out what they are like.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: We usually lose today, because there has been a yesterday, and tomorrow is coming.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: We will burn that bridge when we come to it.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: What by a straight path cannot be reached by crooked ways is never won.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: What is important in life is life, and not the result of life.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: What is my life if I am no longer useful to others.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: What is uttered from the heart alone, Will win the hearts of others to your own.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: What life half gives a man, posterity gives entirely.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: When ideas fail, words come in very handy.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Where is the man who has the strength to be true, and to show himself as he is?
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Which government is the best? The one that teaches us to govern ourselves.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Who is the most sensible person? The one who finds what is to their own advantage in all that happens to them.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Who is the wisest man? He who neither knows or wishes for anything else than what happens.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Whoever wishes to keep a secret must hide the fact that he possesses one.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Wisdom is found only in truth.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Wood burns because it has the proper stuff in it; and a man becomes famous because he has the proper stuff in him.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Things which matter most must never be at the mercy of things which matter least.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: Talent is formed in quiet retreat, character in the headlong rush of life.
quotes.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.quote: The philosophers have only interpreted the world, in various ways: the point, however, is to change it.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Religion is the opiate of the masses.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Sell a man a fish, he eats for a day, teach a man how to fish, you ruin a wonderful business opportunity.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: The production of too many useful things results in too many useless people.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Reason has always existed, but not always in a reasonable form.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Social progress can be measured by the social position of the female sex.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Democracy is the road to socialism.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: All I know is that I am not a Marxist.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Workers of the world unite! You have nothing to lose but your chains.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: It is not the consciousness of men that determines their being, but, on the contrary, their social being that determines their consciousness.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Communism is the riddle of history solved, and it knows itself to be this solution.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Surround yourself with people who make you happy. People who make you laugh, who help you when you're in need. People who genuinely care. They are the ones worth keeping in your life. Everyone else is just passing through.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: The task is not just to understand the world but to change it.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: The only antidote to mental suffering is physical pain.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: The conscience of man does not determine his existence, rather his social existence determines his consciousness.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: From each according to his abilities, to each according to his need.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: A commodity appears at first sight an extremely obvious, trivial thing. But its analysis brings out that it is a very strange thing, abounding in metaphysical subtleties and theological niceties.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: A specter is haunting Europe - the specter of communism.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Anyone who knows anything of history knows that great social changes are impossible without feminine upheaval. Social progress can be measured exactly by the social position of the fair sex, the ugly ones included.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Art is always and everywhere the secret confession, and at the same time the immortal movement of its time.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Capital is dead labor, which, vampire-like, lives only by sucking living labor, and lives the more, the more labor it sucks.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Capital is money, capital is commodities. By virtue of it being value, it has acquired the occult ability to add value to itself. It brings forth living offspring, or, at the least, lays golden eggs.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Capital is reckless of the health or length of life of the laborer, unless under compulsion from society.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Capitalist production, therefore, develops technology, and the combining together of various processes into a social whole, only by sapping the original sources of all wealth - the soil and the labourer.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Experience praises the most happy the one who made the most people happy.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: For the bureaucrat, the world is a mere object to be manipulated by him.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Greek philosophy seems to have met with something with which a good tragedy is not supposed to meet, namely, a dull ending.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: History does nothing; it does not possess immense riches, it does not fight battles. It is men, real, living, who do all this.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: History repeats itself, first as tragedy, second as farce.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: In a higher phase of communist society... only then can the narrow horizon of bourgeois right be fully left behind and society inscribe on its banners: from each according to his ability, to each according to his needs.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: In bourgeois society capital is independent and has individuality, while the living person is dependent and has no individuality.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: It is absolutely impossible to transcend the laws of nature. What can change in historically different circumstances is only the form in which these laws expose themselves.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: It is not history which uses men as a means of achieving - as if it were an individual person - its own ends. History is nothing but the activity of men in pursuit of their ends.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Landlords, like all other men, love to reap where they never sowed.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Let the ruling classes tremble at a communist revolution. The proletarians have nothing to lose but their chains. They have a world to win. Workingmen of all countries, unite!
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Machines were, it may be said, the weapon employed by the capitalists to quell the revolt of specialized labor.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Medicine heals doubts as well as diseases.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Men's ideas are the most direct emanations of their material state.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Natural science will in time incorporate into itself the science of man, just as the science of man will incorporate into itself natural science: there will be one science.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Necessity is blind until it becomes conscious. Freedom is the consciousness of necessity.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Nothing can have value without being an object of utility.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: On a level plain, simple mounds look like hills; and the insipid flatness of our present bourgeoisie is to be measured by the altitude of its great intellects.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Religion is the impotence of the human mind to deal with occurrences it cannot understand.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Religion is the sigh of the oppressed creature, the heart of a heartless world, and the soul of soulless conditions. It is the opium of the people.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Revolutions are the locomotives of history.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: Society does not consist of individuals but expresses the sum of interrelations, the relations within which these individuals stand.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: The English have all the material requisites for the revolution. What they lack is the spirit of generalization and revolutionary ardour.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: The country that is more developed industrially only shows, to the less developed, the image of its own future.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: The development of civilization and industry in general has always shown itself so active in the destruction of forests that everything that has been done for their conservation and production is completely insignificant in comparison.
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.quote: The first requisite for the happiness of the people is the abolition of religion.
