quotes.quote: Admiration of the proletariat, like that of dams, power stations, and aeroplanes, is part of the ideology of the machine age.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Advocates of capitalism are very apt to appeal to the sacred principles of liberty, which are embodied in one maxim: The fortunate must not be restrained in the exercise of tyranny over the unfortunate.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Against my will, in the course of my travels, the belief that everything worth knowing was known at Cambridge gradually wore off. In this respect my travels were very useful to me.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: All movements go too far.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Almost everything that distinguishes the modern world from earlier centuries is attributable to science, which achieved its most spectacular triumphs in the seventeenth century.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Anything you're good at contributes to happiness.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Awareness of universals is called conceiving, and a universal of which we are aware is called a concept.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Both in thought and in feeling, even though time be real, to realise the unimportance of time is the gate of wisdom.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Collective fear stimulates herd instinct, and tends to produce ferocity toward those who are not regarded as members of the herd.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Contempt for happiness is usually contempt for other people's happiness, and is an elegant disguise for hatred of the human race.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Conventional people are roused to fury by departure from convention, largely because they regard such departure as a criticism of themselves.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Democracy is the process by which people choose the man who'll get the blame.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Do not fear to be eccentric in opinion, for every opinion now accepted was once eccentric.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Dogmatism and skepticism are both, in a sense, absolute philosophies; one is certain of knowing, the other of not knowing. What philosophy should dissipate is certainty, whether of knowledge or ignorance.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Ethics is in origin the art of recommending to others the sacrifices required for cooperation with oneself.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Every philosophical problem, when it is subjected to the necessary analysis and justification, is found either to be not really philosophical at all, or else to be, in the sense in which we are using the word, logical.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Freedom comes only to those who no longer ask of life that it shall yield them any of those personal goods that are subject to the mutations of time.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Freedom in general may be defined as the absence of obstacles to the realization of desires.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Freedom of opinion can only exist when the government thinks itself secure.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: I believe in using words, not fists. I believe in my outrage knowing people are living in boxes on the street. I believe in honesty. I believe in a good time. I believe in good food. I believe in sex.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: I do not pretend to start with precise questions. I do not think you can start with anything precise. You have to achieve such precision as you can, as you go along.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: I like mathematics because it is not human and has nothing particular to do with this planet or with the whole accidental universe - because, like Spinoza's God, it won't love us in return.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: I remain convinced that obstinate addiction to ordinary language in our private thoughts is one of the main obstacles to progress in philosophy.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: I say quite deliberately that the Christian religion, as organized in its Churches, has been and still is the principal enemy of moral progress in the world.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: I think we ought always to entertain our opinions with some measure of doubt. I shouldn't wish people dogmatically to believe any philosophy, not even mine.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: I would never die for my beliefs because I might be wrong.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: I've made an odd discovery. Every time I talk to a savant I feel quite sure that happiness is no longer a possibility. Yet when I talk with my gardener, I'm convinced of the opposite.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: If any philosopher had been asked for a definition of infinity, he might have produced some unintelligible rigmarole, but he would certainly not have been able to give a definition that had any meaning at all.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: If there were in the world today any large number of people who desired their own happiness more than they desired the unhappiness of others, we could have a paradise in a few years.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: In America everybody is of the opinion that he has no social superiors, since all men are equal, but he does not admit that he has no social inferiors, for, from the time of Jefferson onward, the doctrine that all men are equal applies only upwards, not downwards.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: In the revolt against idealism, the ambiguities of the word experience have been perceived, with the result that realists have more and more avoided the word.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: It has been said that man is a rational animal. All my life I have been searching for evidence which could support this.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: It is possible that mankind is on the threshold of a golden age; but, if so, it will be necessary first to slay the dragon that guards the door, and this dragon is religion.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: It is preoccupation with possessions, more than anything else, that prevents us from living freely and nobly.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: It seems to be the fate of idealists to obtain what they have struggled for in a form which destroys their ideals.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Italy, and the spring and first love all together should suffice to make the gloomiest person happy.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Life is nothing but a competition to be the criminal rather than the victim.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Love is something far more than desire for sexual intercourse; it is the principal means of escape from the loneliness which afflicts most men and women throughout the greater part of their lives.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Machines are worshipped because they are beautiful and valued because they confer power; they are hated because they are hideous and loathed because they impose slavery.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Man is a credulous animal, and must believe something; in the absence of good grounds for belief, he will be satisfied with bad ones.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Many a man will have the courage to die gallantly, but will not have the courage to say, or even to think, that the cause for which he is asked to die is an unworthy one.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Many people when they fall in love look for a little haven of refuge from the world, where they can be sure of being admired when they are not admirable, and praised when they are not praiseworthy.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Many people would sooner die than think; in fact, they do so.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Mathematics may be defined as the subject in which we never know what we are talking about, nor whether what we are saying is true.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Mathematics takes us into the region of absolute necessity, to which not only the actual word, but every possible word, must conform.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Men are born ignorant, not stupid. They are made stupid by education.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Men who are unhappy, like men who sleep badly, are always proud of the fact.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Much that passes as idealism is disguised hatred or disguised love of power.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Neither a man nor a crowd nor a nation can be trusted to act humanely or to think sanely under the influence of a great fear.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Next to enjoying ourselves, the next greatest pleasure consists in preventing others from enjoying themselves, or, more generally, in the acquisition of power.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: No; we have been as usual asking the wrong question. It does not matter a hoot what the mockingbird on the chimney is singing. The real and proper question is: Why is it beautiful?
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: None but a coward dares to boast that he has never known fear.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Obscenity is whatever happens to shock some elderly and ignorant magistrate.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Of all forms of caution, caution in love is perhaps the most fatal to true happiness.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: One should respect public opinion insofar as is necessary to avoid starvation and keep out of prison, but anything that goes beyond this is voluntary submission to an unnecessary tyranny.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Order, unity, and continuity are human inventions, just as truly as catalogues and encyclopedias.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Patriotism is the willingness to kill and be killed for trivial reasons.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Reason is a harmonising, controlling force rather than a creative one.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Religion is something left over from the infancy of our intelligence, it will fade away as we adopt reason and science as our guidelines.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Religions that teach brotherly love have been used as an excuse for persecution, and our profoundest scientific insight is made into a means of mass destruction.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Religions, which condemn the pleasures of sense, drive men to seek the pleasures of power. Throughout history power has been the vice of the ascetic.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Right discipline consists, not in external compulsion, but in the habits of mind which lead spontaneously to desirable rather than undesirable activities.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Sin is geographical.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: So far as I can remember, there is not one word in the Gospels in praise of intelligence.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The coward wretch whose hand and heart Can bear to torture aught below, Is ever first to quail and start From the slightest pain or equal foe.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The demand for certainty is one which is natural to man, but is nevertheless an intellectual vice.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The fact that an opinion has been widely held is no evidence whatever that it is not utterly absurd.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The fundamental concept in social science is Power, in the same sense in which Energy is the fundamental concept in physics.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The fundamental defect of fathers, in our competitive society, is that they want their children to be a credit to them.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The megalomaniac differs from the narcissist by the fact that he wishes to be powerful rather than charming, and seeks to be feared rather than loved. To this type belong many lunatics and most of the great men of history.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The most savage controversies are about matters as to which there is no good evidence either way.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The observer, when he seems to himself to be observing a stone, is really, if physics is to be believed, observing the effects of the stone upon himself.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The only thing that will redeem mankind is cooperation.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The place of the father in the modern suburban family is a very small one, particularly if he plays golf.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The point of philosophy is to start with something so simple as not to seem worth stating, and to end with something so paradoxical that no one will believe it.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The secret of happiness is this: let your interests be as wide as possible, and let your reactions to the things and persons that interest you be as far as possible friendly rather than hostile.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The secret to happiness is to face the fact that the world is horrible.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The slave is doomed to worship time and fate and death, because they are greater than anything he finds in himself, and because all his thoughts are of things which they devour.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The theoretical understanding of the world, which is the aim of philosophy, is not a matter of great practical importance to animals, or to savages, or even to most civilised men.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The true spirit of delight, the exaltation, the sense of being more than Man, which is the touchstone of the highest excellence, is to be found in mathematics as surely as poetry.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The universe may have a purpose, but nothing we know suggests that, if so, this purpose has any similarity to ours.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The whole problem with the world is that fools and fanatics are always so certain of themselves, and wiser people so full of doubts.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: There is no need to worry about mere size. We do not necessarily respect a fat man more than a thin man. Sir Isaac Newton was very much smaller than a hippopotamus, but we do not on that account value him less.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: There is something feeble and a little contemptible about a man who cannot face the perils of life without the help of comfortable myths.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Those who forget good and evil and seek only to know the facts are more likely to achieve good than those who view the world through the distorting medium of their own desires.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Thought is subversive and revolutionary, destructive and terrible, Thought is merciless to privilege, established institutions, and comfortable habit. Thought is great and swift and free.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: To acquire immunity to eloquence is of the utmost importance to the citizens of a democracy.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: To be without some of the things you want is an indispensable part of happiness.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: To conquer fear is the beginning of wisdom.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: To teach how to live without certainty and yet without being paralysed by hesitation is perhaps the chief thing that philosophy, in our age, can do for those who study it.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: To understand a name you must be acquainted with the particular of which it is a name.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: War does not determine who is right - only who is left.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: We are faced with the paradoxical fact that education has become one of the chief obstacles to intelligence and freedom of thought.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: When the intensity of emotional conviction subsides, a man who is in the habit of reasoning will search for logical grounds in favour of the belief which he finds in himself.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Why is propaganda so much more successful when it stirs up hatred than when it tries to stir up friendly feeling?
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: With the introduction of agriculture mankind entered upon a long period of meanness, misery, and madness, from which they are only now being freed by the beneficent operation of the machine.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Work is of two kinds: first, altering the position of matter at or near the earth's surface relative to other matter; second, telling other people to do so.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Bad philosophers may have a certain influence; good philosophers, never.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Few people can be happy unless they hate some other person, nation, or creed.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Happiness is not best achieved by those who seek it directly.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Hatred of enemies is easier and more intense than love of friends. But from men who are more anxious to injure opponents than to benefit the world at large no great good is to be expected.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The life of man is a long march through the night, surrounded by invisible foes, tortured by weariness and pain, towards a goal that few can hope to reach, and where none may tarry long.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: The root of the matter the thing I mean is love, Christian love, or compassion. If you feel this, you have a motive for existence, a guide for action, a reason for courage, an imperative necessity for intellectual honesty.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: To be happy in this world, especially when youth is past, it is necessary to feel oneself not merely an isolated individual whose day will soon be over, but part of the stream of life slowing on from the first germ to the remote and unknown future.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: What else is there to make life tolerable? We stand on the shore of an ocean, crying to the night and to emptiness. Sometimes a voice of one drowning, and in a moment the silence returns. The world seems to me quite dreadful, the unhappiness of many people is very great, and I often wonder how they all endure it. It is usually the central thing around which their lives are built, and I suppose if they did not live most of their lives in the things of the moment, they would not be able to go on.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: One of the symptoms of approaching nervous breakdown is the belief that one's work is terribly important, and that to take a holiday would bring all kinds of disaster.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: "Change" is scientific, "progress" is ethical; change is indubitable, whereas progress is a matter of controversy.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: No nation was ever so virtuous as each believes itself, and none was ever so wicked as each believes the other.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: We have in fact, two kinds of morality, side by side: one which we preach, but do not practise, and another which we practise, but seldom preach.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: No one gossips about other people's secret virtues.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: In all affairs it's a healthy thing now and then to hang a question mark on the things you have long taken for granted.
quotes.author: Bertrand Russell

quotes.quote: Eloquence: the art of saying things in such a way that those to whom we speak may listen to them with pleasure.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Imagination decides everything.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Noble deeds that are concealed are most esteemed.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: We are conscious of beauty when there is a harmonious relation between something in our nature and the quality of the object which delights us.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Men are so necessarily mad, that not to be mad would amount to another form of madness.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Cleopatra's nose had it been shorter, the whole aspect of the world would have been altered.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The stream is always pure at its source.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: I have discovered that all the unhappiness of men arises from one single fact, that they cannot stay quiet in their own chamber.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The human being is the weakest reed in the world, but it is a reed that thinks.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: When the universe has crushed him, the human being will still be nobler than that which kills him, because he knows that he is dying, and of its victory the universe knows nothing.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: A trifle consoles us, for a trifle distresses us.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: All of our reasoning ends in surrender to feeling.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: As men are not able to fight against death, misery, ignorance, they have taken it into their heads, in order to be happy, not to think of them at all.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Atheism shows strength of mind, but only to a certain degree.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Belief is a wise wager. Granted that faith cannot be proved, what harm will come to you if you gamble on its truth and it proves false? If you gain, you gain all; if you lose, you lose nothing. Wager, then, without hesitation, that He exists.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Between us and heaven or hell there is only life, which is the frailest thing in the world.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Can anything be stupider than that a man has the right to kill me because he lives on the other side of a river and his ruler has a quarrel with mine, though I have not quarrelled with him?
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Chance gives rise to thoughts, and chance removes them; no art can keep or acquire them.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Continuous eloquence wearies. Grandeur must be abandoned to be appreciated. Continuity in everything is unpleasant. Cold is agreeable, that we may get warm.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Contradiction is not a sign of falsity, nor the lack of contradiction a sign of truth.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Custom is our nature. What are our natural principles but principles of custom?
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Desire and force between them are responsible for all our actions; desire causes our voluntary acts, force our involuntary.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Do you wish people to think well of you? Don't speak well of yourself.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Earnestness is enthusiasm tempered by reason.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Eloquence is a painting of the thoughts.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Even those who write against fame wish for the fame of having written well, and those who read their works desire the fame of having read them.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Evil is easy, and has infinite forms.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Faith embraces many truths which seem to contradict each other.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Faith is different from proof; the latter is human, the former is a Gift from God.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Few friendships would survive if each one knew what his friend says of him behind his back.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Habit is a second nature that destroys the first. But what is nature? Why is habit not natural? I am very much afraid that nature itself is only a first habit, just as habit is a second nature.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: He that takes truth for his guide, and duty for his end, may safely trust to God's providence to lead him aright.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Human beings must be known to be loved; but Divine beings must be loved to be known.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: I can well conceive a man without hands, feet, head. But I cannot conceive man without thought; he would be a stone or a brute.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: I have discovered that all human evil comes from this, man's being unable to sit still in a room.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: I have made this letter longer than usual, only because I have not had the time to make it shorter.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: If all men knew what others say of them, there would not be four friends in the world.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: If man made himself the first object of study, he would see how incapable he is of going further. How can a part know the whole?
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: If our condition were truly happy, we would not seek diversion from it in order to make ourselves happy.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: If we examine our thoughts, we shall find them always occupied with the past and the future.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: If we must not act save on a certainty, we ought not to act on religion, for it is not certain. But how many things we do on an uncertainty, sea voyages, battles!
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: If you gain, you gain all. If you lose, you lose nothing. Wager then, without hesitation, that He exists.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: In each action we must look beyond the action at our past, present, and future state, and at others whom it affects, and see the relations of all those things. And then we shall be very cautious.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: In faith there is enough light for those who want to believe and enough shadows to blind those who don't.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: It is natural for the mind to believe and for the will to love; so that, for want of true objects, they must attach themselves to false.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: It is not good to be too free. It is not good to have everything one wants.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: It is the heart which perceives God and not the reason. That is what faith is: God perceived by the heart, not by the reason.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Jesus is the God whom we can approach without pride and before whom we can humble ourselves without despair.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Justice and power must be brought together, so that whatever is just may be powerful, and whatever is powerful may be just.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Justice is what is established; and thus all our established laws will necessarily be regarded as just without examination, since they are established.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Justice without force is powerless; force without justice is tyrannical.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Law, without force, is impotent.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Love has reasons which reason cannot understand.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Man is but a reed, the most feeble thing in nature, but he is a thinking reed.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Man's true nature being lost, everything becomes his nature; as, his true good being lost, everything becomes his good.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Men blaspheme what they do not know.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Men despise religion. They hate it and are afraid it may be true.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Men never do evil so completely and cheerfully as when they do it from religious conviction.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Men often take their imagination for their heart; and they believe they are converted as soon as they think of being converted.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Nature is an infinite sphere of which the center is everywhere and the circumference nowhere.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Nothing fortifies scepticism more than the fact that there are some who are not sceptics; if all were so, they would be wrong.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Nothing gives rest but the sincere search for truth.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Nothing is as approved as mediocrity, the majority has established it and it fixes it fangs on whatever gets beyond it either way.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Nothing is so intolerable to man as being fully at rest, without a passion, without business, without entertainment, without care.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: One must know oneself. If this does not serve to discover truth, it at least serves as a rule of life and there is nothing better.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Our nature consists in motion; complete rest is death.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Our soul is cast into a body, where it finds number, time, dimension. Thereupon it reasons, and calls this nature necessity, and can believe nothing else.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: People are usually more convinced by reasons they discovered themselves than by those found by others.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Reason commands us far more imperiously than a master; for in disobeying the one we are unfortunate, and in disobeying the other we are fools.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Since we cannot know all that there is to be known about anything, we ought to know a little about everything.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: That we must love one God only is a thing so evident that it does not require miracles to prove it.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The charm of fame is so great that we like every object to which it is attached, even death.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The consciousness of the falsity of present pleasures, and the ignorance of the vanity of absent pleasures, cause inconstancy.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The eternal silence of these infinite spaces frightens me.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The finite is annihilated in the presence of the infinite, and becomes a pure nothing. So our spirit before God, so our justice before divine justice.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The gospel to me is simply irresistible.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The greater intellect one has, the more originality one finds in men. Ordinary persons find no difference between men.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The greatness of man is great in that he knows himself to be wretched. A tree does not know itself to be wretched.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The immortality of the soul is a matter which is of so great consequence to us and which touches us so profoundly that we must have lost all feeling to be indifferent about it.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The knowledge of God is very far from the love of Him.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The last act is bloody, however pleasant all the rest of the play is: a little earth is thrown at last upon our head, and that is the end forever.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The last proceeding of reason is to recognize that there is an infinity of things which are beyond it. There is nothing so conformable to reason as this disavowal of reason.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The only shame is to have none.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The self is hateful.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The sensitivity of men to small matters, and their indifference to great ones, indicates a strange inversion.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The strength of a man's virtue should not be measured by his special exertions, but by his habitual acts.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The supreme function of reason is to show man that some things are beyond reason.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: The weather and my mood have little connection. I have my foggy and my fine days within me; my prosperity or misfortune has little to do with the matter.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: There are only two kinds of men: the righteous who think they are sinners and the sinners who think they are righteous.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: There are some who speak well and write badly. For the place and the audience warm them, and draw from their minds more than they think of without that warmth.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: There are two kinds of people one can call reasonable: those who serve God with all their heart because they know him, and those who seek him with all their heart because they do not know him.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: There is a God shaped vacuum in the heart of every man which cannot be filled by any created thing, but only by God, the Creator, made known through Jesus.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Through space the universe encompasses and swallows me up like an atom; through thought I comprehend the world.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Thus so wretched is man that he would weary even without any cause for weariness... and so frivolous is he that, though full of a thousand reasons for weariness, the least thing, such as playing billiards or hitting a ball, is sufficient enough to amuse him.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Time heals griefs and quarrels, for we change and are no longer the same persons. Neither the offender nor the offended are any more themselves.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: To have no time for philosophy is to be a true philosopher.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Too much and too little wine. Give him none, he cannot find truth; give him too much, the same.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Truly it is an evil to be full of faults; but it is a still greater evil to be full of them and to be unwilling to recognize them, since that is to add the further fault of a voluntary illusion.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Truth is so obscure in these times, and falsehood so established, that, unless we love the truth, we cannot know it.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Two things control men's nature, instinct and experience.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Vanity is but the surface.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Vanity of science. Knowledge of physical science will not console me for ignorance of morality in time of affliction, but knowledge of morality will always console me for ignorance of physical science.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: We are only falsehood, duplicity, contradiction; we both conceal and disguise ourselves from ourselves.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: We like security: we like the pope to be infallible in matters of faith, and grave doctors to be so in moral questions so that we can feel reassured.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: We never love a person, but only qualities.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: We only consult the ear because the heart is wanting.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: We run carelessly to the precipice, after we have put something before us to prevent us seeing it.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: We sail within a vast sphere, ever drifting in uncertainty, driven from end to end.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: We view things not only from different sides, but with different eyes; we have no wish to find them alike.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: When we are in love we seem to ourselves quite different from what we were before.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: When we see a natural style, we are astonished and charmed; for we expected to see an author, and we find a person.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: Words differently arranged have a different meaning, and meanings differently arranged have different effects.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: You always admire what you really don't understand.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: I cannot forgive Descartes; in all his philosophy he did his best to dispense with God. But he could not avoid making Him set the world in motion with a flick of His finger; after that he had no more use for God.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.quote: A coward turns away, but a brave man's choice is danger.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: A just cause needs no interpreting. It carries its own case. But the unjust argument since it is sick, needs clever medicine.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: A rare spoil for a man Is the winning of a good wife; very Plentiful are the worthless women.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: A second wife is hateful to the children of the first; A viper is not more hateful.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: A sharp-tempered woman, or, for that matter, a man, Is easier to deal with than the clever type Who holds her tongue.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: A wise man in his house should find a wife gentle and courteous, or no wife at all.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: All men know their children Mean more than life. If childless people sneer- Well, they've less sorrow. But what lonesome luck!
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Cowards do not count in battle; they are there, but not in it.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: In adverse hours the friendship of the good shines most; each prosperous day commands its friends.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: In case of dissension, never dare to judge till you've heard the other side.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: In every work a reward added makes the pleasure twice as great.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: In the hands of vicious men, a mob will do anything. But under good leaders it's quite a different story.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: It is a strange form of anger, difficult to cure, when two friends turn upon each other in hatred.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: It is better that we live ever so Miserably than die in glory.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: It is the wise man's part to leave in darkness everything that is ugly.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: It is wise to withhold one's heart and mind from men who think themselves superior.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: It's folly that women measure their happiness with the pleasures of the bed, but they do. And when the pleasure cools or their man goes missing, all they once lived for turns dark and hateful.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: It's not beauty but fine qualities, my girl, that keep a husband.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Joint undertakings stand a better chance when they benefit both sides.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Keep alive the light of justice, and much that men say in blame will pass you by.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Life is a short affair; We should try to make it smooth, and free from strife.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Life is short; this being so, who would pursue great things and not bear with what is at hand? These are the ways of madmen and men of evil counsel, at least in my judgment.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Light be the earth upon you, lightly rest.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Love is all we have, the only way that each can help the other.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Love must not touch the marrow of the soul. Our affections must be breakable chains that we can cast them off or tighten them....
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Lucky that man whose children make his happiness in life and not his grief, the anguished disappointment of his hopes.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Man's best possession is a sympathetic wife.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Men hate the haughty of heart who will not be the friend of every man.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Men honor property above all else; it has the greatest power in human life.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Men say of us that we live a life free from danger at home while they fight wars. How wrong they are! I would rather stand three times in the battle line than bear one child.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Mighty is geometry; joined with art, resistless.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Mobs in their emotions are much like children, subject to the same tantrums and fits of fury.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: My tongue swore, but my mind was still unpledged.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Neither earth nor ocean produces a creature as savage and monstrous as woman.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Never say that marriage has more of joy than pain.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: No man on earth is truly free, All are slaves of money or necessity. Public opinion or fear of prosecution forces each one, against his conscience, to conform.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: No one can confidently say that he will still be living tomorrow.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Numbers are a fearful thing, and joined to craft a desperate foe.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: O lady, nobility is thine, and thy form is the reflection of thy nature!
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: O sleep's enchantment, friend and helper against sickness.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Of all things upon earth that bleed and grow, a herb most bruised is woman.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Of mortals there is no one who is happy. If wealth flows in upon one, one may be perhaps luckier than one's neighbor, but still not happy.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.quote: Oh, what a vileness human beauty is; corroding, corrupting everything it touches.
quotes.author: Euripides

quotes.author: Mother Teresa

quotes.author: Mother Teresa

quotes.quote: Instead of death and sorrow, let us bring peace and joy to the world.

quotes.quote: Life is an opportunity, benefit from it. Life is beauty, admire it. Life is bliss, taste it. Life is a dream, realise it. Life is a challenge, meet it. Life is duty, complete it. Life is love, enjoy it. Life is mystery, know it. Life is a promise, fulfil it. Life is a sorrow, overcome it. Life is a song, sing it. Life is a struggle, accept it. Life is an adventure, dares it. quotes.author: Mother Teresa

quotes.quote: In the silence of our hearts, God speaks, and from the fullness of our hearts we speak.

quotes.author: Steve Jobs

quotes.quote: That's what makes great products. It's not process-it's content.

quotes.quote: We used to dream about this stuff. Now we get to build it. It's pretty great.

quotes.author: Steve Jobs

quotes.quote: Design is not just what it looks like and feels like. Design is how it works.

quotes.quote: Older people sit down and ask, 'What is it?' but the boy asks, 'What can I do with it?'.

quotes.quote: That's been one of my mantras - focus and simplicity. Simple can be harder than complex: You have to work hard to get your thinking clean to make it simple. But it's worth it in the end, because once you get there, you can move mountains.

quotes.quote: Have the courage to follow your heart and intuition. They somehow already know what you truly want to become.

quotes.quote: From almost the beginning at Apple we were, for some incredibly lucky reason, fortunate enough to be at the right place at the right time.

quotes.quote: I was lucky—I found what I love to do early in life.

quotes.quote: Quality is more important than quantity. One home run is much better than two doubles.

quotes.author: Steve Jobs

quotes.quote: In business, if I knew earlier what I know now, I'd have probably done some things a lot better than I did, but I also would've probably done some other things a lot worse. But so what? It's more important to be engaged in the present.

quotes.quote: We hire people who want to make the best things in the world.
quotes.author: Steve Jobs

quotes.quote: Technology is nothing. What's important is that you have a faith in people, that they're basically good and smart, and if you give them tools, they'll do wonderful things with them.
quotes.author: Steve Jobs

quotes.quote: Do your best at every job. Don't sleep! Success generates more success so be hungry for it. Hire good people with a passion for excellence.
quotes.author: Steve Jobs

quotes.quote: We're trying to make great products for people, and we at least have the courage of our convictions to say 'We don't think this is part of what makes a great product, we're going to leave it out.' That's what a lot of customers pay us to do.
quotes.author: Steve Jobs

quotes.quote: When you're a carpenter making a beautiful chest of drawers, you're not going to use a piece of plywood on the back, even though it faces the wall and nobody will ever see it.
